absent: Exact numeric encodings for destination modes, allocation type tags and vector identifiers beyond the identifier width and maximum stated in findings.
Mapping from IOAPIC pin numbers to global system interrupts and trigger attribute sources.
Internal behavior of parent domain allocation, activation and message composition helpers.
Detailed ordering between IOAPIC programming and vector assignment outside the stated guards.
Timer period, callback actions and reclamation policy for deferred vector cleanup.
Platform hook behavior for default PCI message domain publication and virtualization restore path.
Legacy interrupt count and legacy controller masking semantics.
Maintenance of online, present and once booted processor sets.
Controller register layout and idle polling bounds for shortcut delivery.
Remapping write path and hardware message format for remapping messages.

findings.text: This dossier owns an interrupt domain for IOAPIC pins that offers four lifecycle operations covering creation, release, programming and masking, invoked by the generic layer as interrupts are managed.

Creation succeeds only for a single interrupt with valid placement information, an existing software descriptor and an unused hardware pin; larger batches, missing information and duplicate mappings are rejected, with parent allocation and private storage unwound on failure.

Newly created routing state starts cleared, then records trigger mode and polarity from the private attributes; level sensitive lines begin masked while edge sensitive lines rely on core handling for masking after arrival.

On success the allocation guarantees legacy controller masking for low virtual numbers, linkage of pin to node, recorded trigger attributes, initialized routing state, level aware handler registration, and chip behavior selected from the parent domain alongside the bound hardware pin.
Release is defined only for a single interrupt and combines upper layer teardown with disposal of private storage, detachment of the pin association and a warning when any linkage survives.
The IOAPIC instance number for a domain is carried opaquely in the domain host private field and recovered by integer conversion.

Programming of an entry during activation occurs while holding the IOAPIC guard; deactivation only masks the entry and is never invoked for interrupts that aggregate multiple pins, while legacy masking during creation runs with local delivery suppressed.

Broadcast acceleration moves between disabled and enabled states; it stays disabled when forced off, when only one processor is online or when some present processor never booted, and becomes enabled only after all those conditions clear, protecting early boot from stray broadcasts.
Early boot accepts a numeric option controlling shorthand broadcasts and later reports the resulting broadcast mode during initialization.

Single processor configurations suppress all but self delivery; with multiple processors the implementation prefers hardware broadcast when the toggle allows it and otherwise iterates over the online set, with call function delivery additionally distinguishing whether the caller is included and whether the target set covers all online processors.

Requesting rescheduling of an offline processor warns and drops the request, while nonmaskable delivery to an offline processor requires driver support and evidence of a prior boot, warning when either requirement is absent.

Shortcut delivery first ensures the controller is idle, using a bounded wait for nonmaskable vectors and an unbounded wait otherwise, then issues a combined shortcut and vector command for which destination fields are ignored.

Physical destination delivery resolves each target processor through a per processor hardware identifier table and supports single, sequential mask and all but self mask variants, with the latter skipping the initiating processor.

Logical destination delivery encodes targets as bit positions for sequential and all but self iteration, skips the initiator in the all but self form, and for combined mask delivery transmits the whole online subset as one mask while warning when offline processors are included and doing nothing for an empty set.
All physical and logical single and mask delivery loops suppress local interrupt delivery for the duration of the destination iteration, restoring the prior state afterwards.
Default single, all, all but self and self delivery are thin wrappers over either mask transmission or hardware shortcut commands.
The extended controller helper transmits a vector to an explicit hardware identifier with a caller chosen destination mode through a single controller write.

Per interrupt vector state keeps a cached hardware configuration, current and previous vector numbers, current and previous processor assignments, the software interrupt number, cleanup list linkage and four single bit flags recording migration, managed, reservation capable and reservation held conditions.
Vector management keeps a global search mask, a local controller chip descriptor and a matrix allocator object, plus a globally visible vector domain pointer.
Each processor owns cleanup state pairing a list of vectors awaiting reclamation with a pinned timer that drives deferred cleanup.

A dedicated raw spinlock serializes vector assignment and affinity transitions; acquisition blocks changes to the online set during assignment and is released explicitly, with message migration holding it only across the temporary redirection window.

Affinity changes for message signalled interrupts first delegate to the parent layer and then choose between immediate message refresh and a staged transition; the staged path temporarily redirects to the new vector on the current processor, marks an unused vector to suppress missing handler warnings, completes the move to the final target and retriggers when the controller shows the vector pending.

Immediate message refresh is allowed when reservation is unavailable, when the vector is unchanged, during startup with a shutdown vector, before startup, or when the destination processor is unchanged; otherwise the staged transition applies and the current processor is expected to be the migration initiator.

Non atomic address and data updates can raise a stray interrupt on the new vector during migration; the design tolerates it as spurious when a handler exists and pre marks unused vectors to avoid missing handler reports.
Message refresh composes a two slot message from the cached target configuration and hands it to the parent chip write operation.

Device message setup validates that the real parent uses a supported bus family and that the target uses a PCI message flavour, intersects requested feature flags with parent support, enforces required flags, installs preparation and chip operations for acknowledgement, retrigger and affinity, and selects edge handling.

PCI message domain creation is skipped when the controller is disabled; otherwise the vector domain is promoted to a message parent with the vector parent operations and published as the default PCI message domain through the platform hook.
Preparation distinguishes extended versus base PCI message types from device or bus token state, initializes generic allocation information and rejects unsupported bus families.

Remapping messages use an edge triggered controller offering mask, unmask, acknowledgement, affinity, retrigger, compose and write operations, with compose deriving the message from cached target state in remapped form and write forwarding through the remapping write path.
Creation of the remapping domain singleton is serialized by a dedicated mutex with reuse after first success, backed by a named firmware node that is released when domain creation fails.

Remapping allocation requests a single interrupt bound to a caller identifier carried as device, hardware and private data, failing when the domain is unavailable, with a symmetric single interrupt release.
Restoration of message interrupts delegates to the virtualization aware helper and reports its outcome.

Thirty two bit controller selection honours an explicit command line driver name when it matches a registered driver and otherwise probes registered drivers in order, installing the first that claims the hardware and failing boot when none claims it.

The default thirty two bit controller descriptor declares a name, always successful probe, logical destination mode, loader and present mapping helpers, physical and logical delivery operations including mask and broadcast forms, and memory mapped access with distinct idle and bounded idle waits, installed as the initial global controller.

Hardware identifier decoding shifts the version register value by twenty four bits and keeps eight bits on extended capable hardware versus four bits otherwise, with an architectural maximum of two hundred fifty four.
Including offline processors in a combined logical mask triggers a warning, indicating a caller error that still proceeds to hardware.
